signals.title: USD — Fed Hawkish Pivot + Jackson Hole Repricing
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.77 while the DXY holds at 99.58, supported by Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks which shifted market expectations toward a September hike. Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% provides a +275bp carry advantage, now reinforced by hike odds rising to 57% following Warsh’s speech. Despite the hawkish pivot, USD ESI at -10.2 suggests recent data has disappointed, creating a dependency on the upcoming payrolls to validate the higher-for-longer narrative. The DXY remains positioned above its SMA20 (99.49) but below the SMA50 (100.42), indicating a constructive but not yet breakout technical profile. Trade bias: Bullish USD; Fed hawkish repricing supports the greenback against lower-yielding peers. Catalyst: US August Jobs data on Friday. Risk: Disappointing employment figures force a reversal of the Jackson Hole hike bets.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing the 160.00 threshold again after a brief dip, following headlines that confirmed a break past this level previously triggered record joint intervention. JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 (pctl 9) remains deeply crowded, yet 25d risk reversals show a strong -1.74 put skew, signaling that the options market is paying heavily for downside protection. Curiously, USD/JPY VRP is negative at -1.6%, with IV at 7.2% trailing HV30 at 8.8%, suggesting realized volatility is outpacing option premiums despite the acute policy risk. This divergence indicates a potential for a volatility spike if the MoF/BoJ steps in to defend the 160 level. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; intervention risk at 160.00 caps upside regardless of carry. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 without MoF response invites further spec selling.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5920, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.591/0.581/0.585) ahead of the RBNZ policy decision. COT LF net positioning has reached an extreme short at -32,496 (pctl 0, z -2.60), representing a complete lack of speculative support. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. While Fed hawkishness provides a USD tailwind, the NZD speculative vacuum leaves the pair asymmetric to the upside on any hawkish RBNZ communication. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze potential against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: RBNZ adopts a dovish hold, validating the record spec short position.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD holds at 0.7169, staying above its SMA200 at 0.6971, but faces significant positioning headwinds. COT LF net long +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92) shows institutional positioning is at its most crowded level in a year, while retail sentiment is 87% short, creating a sharp institutional-vs-retail divergence. A -71bp OIS carry deficit (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) favors the AUD, yet the inability of price to extend higher despite the carry lead and retail fading suggests the trend is exhausting. AUD ESI is neutral at +1.4, offering no fresh macro catalyst to justify further institutional adds at these levels. Trade bias: Neutral/Short AUD/USD; crowded institutional longs are vulnerable to a profit-taking correction. Catalyst: Australian GDP data. Risk: RBA unexpectedly shifts hawkish, forcing retail capitulation and a further leg higher.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3545, currently below its SMA20 of 1.354 but holding above the SMA50/200 support zone. The pair exhibits a massive +6.1% Vol Risk Premium, with ATM IV at 11.0% against realized HV30 of 4.9%, the highest premium in the G10 space. This suggests the options market is pricing in extreme uncertainty following Warsh's speech, despite speculative positioning already being crowded long (pctl 96, z +1.58). The BoE-Fed carry is neutral at 0bp, leaving Cable sensitive to US yield shifts and domestic data disappointments as evidenced by the negative GBP ESI of -9.2. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol premium and crowded long positioning limit the appeal of chasing the trend. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: Technical break below the SMA200 (1.3439) triggers a broad speculative unwind.
